item.text: {"text":"Evidence supports testing the objective before replacing history aggregation. [gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec weaknesses to overconfidence from sampled BCE; more negatives plus generalized BCE improve results without changing the backbone. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies a strong combination using SASRec’s training task and sampled softmax, although its Transformer layers also change. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (2025)](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides SASRec implementations comparing uniform, in-batch, mixed-negative and full-softmax training. Nonuniform sampling needs correction matched to the actual sampling scheme. A [2024 negative-sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds uniform sampling favors head items, while popularity-based negatives can balance popularity bands at an aggregate-accuracy cost.\n\nFalse-negative safeguards are promising but require ablation. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090) combines refreshed memory-bank negatives with ID exclusion and similarity-window filtering; its reported datasets do not establish benefits for Electronics. [TCA4Rec (2025)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40537-025-01184-9) proposes popularity-aware contrastive training, with additional memory and training stages. Practical inference for this budget: retain SASRec; compare multi-negative cross-entropy against gBCE, then uniform versus corrected mixed sampling, masking known training positives and positive-ID collisions. Add weak representation regularization only afterward. Alignment alone cannot establish collapse: inspect centered covariance spectra, effective rank, variance and popularity-stratified performance. None of these results establishes gains on the pinned benchmark; select exclusively by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10, track Electronics separately, and compare GPU cost."}
